title: S.C. Legislation 3
description: This legislation, which I authored and carried through the full approval process, was designed to strengthen transparency and accountability in the Council’s legislative process. It expanded the Rules Committee’s jurisdiction from mere review to formal amendment authority, allowing it to ensure that all proposed legislation met constitutional and formatting standards before Council ratification. I introduced clear procedural requirements mandating that all constitutional and bylaw amendments be reviewed by the Rules Committee prior to voting, thereby closing procedural gaps that had caused confusion in prior sessions. Today, this framework continues to serve as the procedural backbone for how legislation is submitted, reviewed, and enacted in 7CSC.

description: To improve organizational clarity and resolve systemic inconsistencies across the Council’s membership structure, I authored and passed this comprehensive amendment that reorganized and standardized all representative positions within 7CSC’s governing documents. The legislation alphabetized all Title II positions, corrected inconsistent naming conventions between elected and appointed members, and added several missing representative roles, including the Student Health and Well-Being Representative and the Student Transportation Representative. title: S.C. Legislation 5b
description: As Speaker, I identified the absence of a formal mechanism for amending the Council’s Constitution as a major procedural vulnerability. To address this, I authored and successfully passed Legislation 5B, which introduced a dedicated amendments clause outlining the conditions and thresholds required for future constitutional changes. The reform established a three-fourths supermajority requirement, delegated limited formatting authority to the Rules Committee, and required all amendments to undergo formal introduction and review before ratification. This legislation remains one of the most structurally important pieces passed during my tenure, creating the legal and procedural foundation for all future constitutional revisions.

title: Charter of the Elevator Special Committee for Advocacy & Petition
description: I co-authored the Charter establishing the Elevator Special Committee for Advocacy & Petition, an ad hoc body formed under the Seventh College Student Council to address persistent elevator failures that affected accessibility and safety for residents. Serving as a committee member, I focused on the digital and data infrastructure underpinning the initiative—designing QR reporting systems and conducting statistical analyses of maintenance response times. Following our presentation, HDH acknowledged the procedural lapse and began improving their elevator issue reporting protocols. The initiative exemplified how targeted data analysis and digital tools can drive tangible institutional change within university systems.

title: Automation & Data Tools Suite
description:
To streamline alumni engagement operations for UC San Diego’s Alumni Department—and to empower future student workers who aren’t code-heavy—I built a reusable toolkit of Google Sheets workflows powered by Google Apps Script custom functions. The suite replaces brittle manual processes with auditable, spreadsheet-native utilities that scale across teams. 

Key capabilities include:
- Record hygiene & merge logic: DUPE_DETECTOR and IMPUTATION_UNIQUE flag adjacent duplicates and impute sparse rows.
- Cross-sheet assembly: GET_SHEET and COLUMN_STACK fetch standardized ranges and stack named columns.
- Flexible lookups: MULTI_SEARCH and HASH_MAP_LOOKUP enable many-to-many mapping beyond VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP.
- Similarity & cleaning: CHAR_SIM, MOST_SIMILAR, and F_FILL provide fuzzy matching and forward-fill capabilities.
- Analytics utilities: CUMLATIVE_SUM, PARTITION_GROUPS, and JOIN_UNIQUE extend Sheets for grouped aggregation and cohort balancing. 

Together, these tools transformed data prep and reporting into one-cell formulas—cutting turnaround time and enabling non-technical staff to maintain automations without writing code.
